project_type: EchoGuard: camera-free sitting/standing tracker. Python backend (numpy streaming CSI processing, calibration, posture model) + Flask dashboard (plain HTML/CSS/JS) + two ESP-IDF firmware projects (XIAO ESP32-S3 TX/RX, ESP-NOW, channel 11 HT40, 100 Hz)
build_system: Makefile + .venv (Python); ESP-IDF idf.py for firmware (installed at ~/esp/esp-idf, tools in ~/.espressif, activate with `. $HOME/esp/esp-idf/export.sh`; firmware/receiver/build and managed_components already exist, so a rebuild should work offline)
test_framework: pytest in tests/ (conftest.py, csi_synth.py synthetic CSI helper, fixtures/ dir); key suites: test_processing.py, test_calibration.py, test_posture.py, test_posture_api.py, test_csi_parser.py, test_engine.py, test_dashboard.py, test_recording.py, test_simulation.py
build_command: node --check dashboard/static/app.js (JS syntax); firmware: cd firmware/receiver && . $HOME/esp/esp-idf/export.sh && idf.py build (same for firmware/transmitter if touched). NEVER flash: the sandbox cannot open serial ports and the user flashes.
verification_instructions: 1) make test must pass. 2) node --check dashboard/static/*.js. 3) If firmware changed: idf.py build in the changed project(s) must succeed (report if ESP-IDF cannot run in the sandbox). 4) The user's dashboard server is running at http://127.0.0.1:8050 with the OLD code (the user restarts it after Python changes); it can be queried read-only with curl (GET /api/status, /api/posture, /api/calibration/state) but do not POST to it, and do not start/stop it.
snapshot_or_generated_files: None checked in. data/ holds runtime files (data/calibration/*.json, data/posture.sqlite3, data/recordings/<session>/...); do not delete or rewrite the user's existing calibration file data/calibration/office__classic_1a0000000000_ch11-2_len128.json.
setup_instructions: .venv already exists (make setup-offline recreates it without network). No new Python dependencies should be needed (numpy/scipy/pandas/flask/pytest/pyserial only).
environment_constraints: No serial port access from the sandbox; the hardware cannot be exercised by the agent. Real-data evidence available: (a) the user's calibration JSON data/calibration/office__classic_1a0000000000_ch11-2_len128.json (per-step stats and profile means/stds, no raw CSI); (b) a 30 s raw capture of the live link taken by the planner at 18:54 local, while the user was (per the live posture output) probably standing or sitting in the room; activity unknown, not labelled: .agents/tasks/task-csi-resolution-walking-fix/diag_capture_20261024-185452.csv (recording.TAKE_FIELDS columns, raw_line holds the CSI_DATA line; 2922 packets). An empty leftover session dir data/recordings/20261024-185452-diagnostic/ (session.json only, its take was deleted) may be removed.
contribution_requirements: No CONTRIBUTING.md. README.md documents every user-visible behaviour (calibration timeline, detection method, API); keep it in sync. Never use em dashes in written content. Keep the not-a-medical-device / no-accuracy-claims wording. Dashboard has strict CSP: no inline scripts/styles, no CDN.
key_patterns: ROOT-CAUSE EVIDENCE (measured by the planner from the raw capture): the CSI integers in CSI_DATA lines are tiny. Per-subcarrier |I|,|Q| mean 0.1-1.5 LSB, amplitude values only {0,1,1.41,2,2.24,2.83,3,3.16,...}, 36% of valid subcarrier amplitudes are exactly 0, per-packet mean amplitude p5/p50/p95 = 0.92/1.17/1.49, max 17.7. Subcarriers ~6-15 (raw LLTF index) are almost always 0. The live status shows outliers_replaced ~3.7 per packet (Hampel MAD collapses to 0 on integer-valued data and the HAMPEL_FLOOR 1e-3 then flags every 1-LSB step). With amplitudes of 1-3 LSB, a 1-LSB flip is a 30-100% change, so quantisation noise dominates. That explains: the empty-room noise_variance 0.080 / noise_diff 0.062 (vs uncalibrated refs 0.03/0.01), the bimodal empty-room motion score, walking (median 0.98) not scoring above the empty room, and the uncalibrated motion score of 17 while still. Likely firmware cause: firmware/receiver/main/app_main.c has CONFIG_GAIN_CONTROL=1 for ESP32-S3 (line ~92) and print_csi_item() prints (int16_t)(g * it->buf[i]) with g = compensate_gain from esp_csi_gain_ctrl_get_gain_compensation(), relative to an AGC/FFT gain baseline recorded from the first 100 packets after the RX boots (CONFIG_FORCE_GAIN=0). If the current gain differs from that boot-time baseline (e.g. antennas attached / signal 35 dB stronger after the RX booted), g can be far below 1 and the multiply-then-truncate destroys the resolution; g is never printed, so this is a strong hypothesis, not verified. Alternative/additional cause: the CSI auto-scaling (wifi_csi_config_t.manu_scale=false, shift=0) producing small values at strong RSSI. The calibration file confirms the downstream failure: separable=false, thresholds fell back to low 4.37/movement 6.56/rapid 13.12 (from quiet_p95 3.64 inflated by the empty step), so every walking frame was below movement and went to PostureClassifier, whose 3-class diagonal Gaussian softmax (sitting/standing/empty) has no option for 'none of these' and output sitting p=0.97. CODE PATTERNS: backend/processing.py SignalProcessor.process(): valid_subcarrier_amplitudes -> per-packet mean normalisation (amp/mean_amp) -> _hampel (window 7, k 3, MAD*1.4826 floored at HAMPEL_FLOOR) -> _smooth EMA alpha 0.3 -> 1 s window; compute_frame() gives variance (mean temporal std), diff_energy (RMS first difference at packet rate), baseline_deviation, motion_score = 0.5*(variance/var_ref + diff/diff_ref); MotionFrame dataclass carries quality_ok/quality_reasons (Q_* reason-code prefixes). backend/calibration.py: StepSpec/STEPS, StepData, step_problems, compute_calibration (thresholds, SEPARATION_RATIO 1.5, conservative fallback with warning), build_posture_model (posture.STEP_CLASSES maps step keys to classes), CalibrationSession (timed run, add_frame from engine frame hook), CalibrationStore, CalibrationManager (start/save/save_result/load/_apply). backend/posture.py: fit_posture_model (per-class mean/std, Fisher top-k=16 sit-vs-stand subcarriers), score_profile/classify_profile (softmax), temporal_self_check, quality_warnings, PostureClassifier.update/_classify with CLASS_STATES {sitting,standing,empty->away}, MOVING_CONFIRM_S, hysteresis via PostureConfig. backend/recording.py: SessionStore/Session/TakeWriter/RecordingManager (start_take(label, duration_s), stop_take, LABELS keys empty_room/standing_still/walking/sitting/...; engine calls the recorder per raw line via set_recorder/_EngineSink). backend/csi_parser.py: parse_line, parse_stats_line (EG_RX_STATS 7 fields, EG_TX_STATS 5 fields), parse_any (unknown lines -> 'other', counted as non_csi_lines). backend/engine.py: Engine.snapshot() builds /api/status (counters, rssi, quality, motion, processing, calibration...), add_status_provider. backend/offline.py: OfflineReplay + apply_calibration_file for replaying recordings through the same pipeline; backend/cli.py has evaluate/monitor/ports subcommands. Tests build synthetic packets with tests/csi_synth.py and use fake clocks; dashboard tests use the Flask test client (tests/test_dashboard.py, tests/test_posture_api.py).
directory_structure: backend/ (pipeline, calibration, posture, sitting tracker, recording, CLI), dashboard/ (Flask server.py + static/ UI), firmware/receiver and firmware/transmitter (ESP-IDF projects), simulation/ (synthetic scenarios), tests/ (pytest), data/ (runtime: config.json, calibration/, recordings/, posture.sqlite3), .agents/tasks/ (task state)
